criterion_notes.c1: The cached PDF contains only the Supplemental Material (blank questionnaires and table headers) for the Bushenyi-Ishaka Municipality WSP study. While Part 1a includes items asking about new connections and supply continuity (hours/day), the main article text is missing, so whether household or community water service access is actually examined cannot be verified.
criterion_notes.c2: Cannot determine without the main article full text. Under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the supplemental instruments reference institutional/governance and regulatory items (such as compliance monitoring plans, NWSC/stakeholder WSP meetings, and an interview prompt on regulatory pressure including environmental law/standards enforcement and municipal by-laws enforcement), which could satisfy broad institutional/regulatory wording if empirically analyzed in the main paper. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, a Water Safety Plan (WSP) is typically an operational drinking-water quality risk-management tool (generic operational/project delivery rather than a rule-type mechanism directly governing service access), and would fail Criterion 2 unless the main paper empirically analyzes how binding regulatory enforcement, municipal by-laws, or utility regulatory rules directly govern water service access or continuity. Because the main text is absent, both readings are unclear.
criterion_notes.c3: Unclear because the retrieved PDF contains only four trailing bibliography entries, blank data-collection questionnaires (Parts 1a and 1b), and unpopulated/unextracted table headers (Parts 2a and 2b), with no main-text methods, sample, or empirical results.
criterion_notes.c4: Unclear. Part 1a lists indicator questions on Supply continuity (average hours/day of supply and supply interruptions exceeding 8 hours) and new connections alongside water quality parameters, but without the main paper it cannot be verified whether access or continuity outcomes are empirically reported.
criterion_notes.c5: Unclear. Because only blank supplemental questionnaires and section titles were retrieved instead of the main article, the study design, respondent/unit sample, analytical exposure, and reported outcomes cannot be identified.
